summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for shortness of breath and left-sided chest pain after missing a dialysis session due to diarrhea. He had used crack cocaine the morning before admission, which contributed to atrial flutter with rapid ventricular response. On arrival, he was hypoxic with bilateral pulmonary edema on chest X-ray and severe hyperkalemia. He was treated with oxygen, started on broad-spectrum antibiotics due to concern for pneumonia, and underwent hemodialysis, which improved his respiratory status and electrolyte abnormalities. His chest pain, reproducible on palpation and associated with tachycardia, improved after removal of his tunneled dialysis catheter and better rate control. His diltiazem dose was increased to 420mg daily taken at noon, and digoxin was adjusted to every other day post-dialysis due to a high trough level. Antibiotics were discontinued after negative blood cultures and clinical improvement. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to adhere to dialysis, avoid cocaine, monitor weight, and follow up with outpatient care.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Combinations of opioid type drug with any other drug dependence, continuous
